$schema_note: Anatomy-based joint range-of-motion envelope for the `anny-tpose-sweep` motion source per RFD 2203. Every entry names the axis, min/max in degrees, and the specific verified public-domain source (document, section, table, page). The sweep's ranges MUST sit inside this envelope; a deliberately hyperextended range fails the gate. When RFD 0007's per-pose validator lands, it also reads this envelope.
envelope_source: NASA RP-1024 Vol.I Chapter VI Tables 1 and 2

licence_verification.verified_via: WebFetch on the NTRS record page 2026-09-04; the excerpt of RP-1024 Vol.II's NTRS record at https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19790005540 carries the same explicit statement
licence_verification.verified_extract: The NTRS record for NASA RP-1024-VOL-1 lists Copyright Status: 'Work of the US Gov. Public Use Permitted.' and Distribution: 'Public'.
licence_verification.table_provenance_caveat: Table 1 reproduces data originally published in Barter, Emanuel and Truett 1957 (a WADC Technical Report — Wright Air Development Center, US Air Force — also a US federal work per 17 USC 105). NASA's reproduction of these tables in RP-1024 is itself PD; the underlying WADC report is PD by the same 17 USC 105 basis. Table 2 was originally verified 2026-09-04 (issue #11): Harris ML. 'A factor analytic study of flexibility.' Research Quarterly 40(1):62-70, March 1969 (PubMed 5252465), published by Taylor & Francis for AAHPER/SHAPE America under subscription — COPYRIGHTED, not PD. NASA cited the 1968 conference presentation of the same work at AAHPER's Research Section, St. Louis. NASA's reproduction remains PD; downstream publication citing the female P5-P95 rows directly should verify against Harris 1969 and comply with Taylor & Francis's licence, or re-source from a PD-clean publication.

axes.percentile_basis: P5-P95 from male data (extension P95 61°, flexion P95 208°) taken as an anatomically-plausible-population envelope; NASA RP-1024 Vol.I Table 1
same as upperarm.L, by anatomical symmetry

axes.sweep_axis_note: hip flexion (thigh forward-up); extension is thigh backward
axes.percentile_basis: P5-P95 from male data (hip extension range indirectly from adduction P95 51°; hip flexion P95 134°); NASA RP-1024 Vol.I Table 1. Hip extension in the male table is not listed as its own row; using -51 as a conservative envelope from adjacent measurements.
P5=92° (voluntary standing) to P95=174° (forced kneeling); NASA RP-1024 Vol.I Table 1 rows 'Knee flexion, voluntary (standing)' and 'Knee flexion forced (kneeling)'

axes.sweep_axis_note: same as knee.L by anatomical symmetry
thoracolumbar spine flexion+extension; RP-1024 female data (male not explicitly tabulated by same row)
axes.percentile_basis: spine extension mean 29° taken as negative side; spine flexion P95 approx mean+SD*1.645 ≈ 76°; NASA RP-1024 Vol.I Table 2 (female data), rows 'Spine flexion' and 'Spine extension'
axes.primary_source_citation: Harris ML. A factor analytic study of flexibility. Research Quarterly 40(1):62-70, March 1969 (PubMed 5252465). Taylor & Francis for AAHPER/SHAPE America.

axes.percentile_basis: P95 approx mean+SD*1.645; NASA RP-1024 Vol.I Table 2 rows 'Neck rotation, right' (mean 83.1°, SD 10.2°) and 'Neck rotation, left' (mean 78.5°, SD 11.2°); ±100° is an inclusive P95 envelope
axes.primary_source_citation: Harris ML. A factor analytic study of flexibility. Research Quarterly 40(1):62-70, March 1969 (PubMed 5252465). Taylor & Francis for AAHPER/SHAPE America.

axes.percentile_basis: P95 approx mean+SD*1.645; NASA RP-1024 Vol.I Table 2 rows 'Neck flexion' (mean 58.7°, SD 10.3°) and 'Neck extension' (mean 89.3°, SD 9.9°); envelope covers -106° (P95 extension) to +76° (P95 flexion)
axes.primary_source_citation: Harris ML. A factor analytic study of flexibility. Research Quarterly 40(1):62-70, March 1969 (PubMed 5252465). Taylor & Francis for AAHPER/SHAPE America.
